content: 1. Recommendation 14.4 has been updated to emphasize the importance of adjusting insulin doses based on the composition of meals consumed by children and adolescents with diabetes. 2. Recommendation 14.10 now includes guidance to screen for psychosocial and behavioral health concerns in children and adolescents with diabetes, with a focus on making appropriate referrals to address these issues. 3. Recommendation 14.53 has been revised to recommend a weight loss goal of 7-10% for youth diagnosed with type 2 diabetes to improve their metabolic health. 4. Recommendations 14.68 and 14.70 have been updated to suggest considering the use of empagliflozin as a treatment option before intensifying insulin therapy in children with type 2 diabetes. 5. Recommendation 14.69 advises healthcare providers to take into account medication adherence and the potential effects of medications on weight when managing youth with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes. 6. Recommendation 14.72 has replaced the term “severe obesity” with “class 2 obesity or higher,” defined as a BMI of ≥ 35 kg/m² or 120% of the 95th percentile for age and sex, to provide a more precise framework for identifying adolescents who may be candidates for metabolic surgery. 7. Recommendation 14.78 has been updated to specify appropriate protein intake levels for children with nephropathy, tailored to their age. 8. New recommendations 14.106 and 14.107 strongly discourage the initiation of smoking, including both tobacco and e-cigarettes, in youth with diabetes. 9. The section on transitioning from pediatric to adult care has been revised to underscore the importance of interprofessional teams in facilitating this process. It emphasizes the need for coordinated care between pediatric specialists and caregivers to determine the optimal timing for transitioning to adult diabetes care.
